title: Greek Prawn Saganaki with Feta & Lemon Orzo
description: King prawns in a chilli-oregano tomato sauce, finished under the grill with crumbled feta, over lemony orzo. Garlic-free.

ingredients.name: Raw peeled king prawns (frozen is fine — thaw overnight in the fridge)
Fresh dill or flat-leaf parsley, chopped

steps.title: Start the sauce
steps.text: Heat 1½ tbsp olive oil in an ovenproof frying pan over medium heat. Soften the onion with a pinch of salt for 6 min, then stir in the oregano and chilli flakes for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Simmer the tomato
steps.text: Add the passata and 100 ml water, season with ½ tsp salt and simmer 10 min until slightly thickened. Bring the 1.5 l salted water to the boil for the orzo meanwhile.

steps.title: Cook the orzo
steps.text: Cook the orzo in the boiling water for 9 min. Drain and toss with the remaining olive oil (about 1½ tsp), the lemon zest and half the lemon juice.

steps.title: Poach the prawns
steps.text: Heat the grill to high. Pat the prawns dry, stir them into the sauce and cook 3 min until just turning pink (they finish under the grill).

steps.title: Grill with feta
steps.text: Scatter the feta over the top and slide the pan under the grill for 4 min, until the feta is soft and golden at the edges and the prawns are cooked through. No ovenproof pan? Tip into a baking dish first.

steps.title: Finish and split
steps.text: Squeeze over the remaining lemon juice and scatter with dill. Matthias: ≈420 g prawns with 70 g feta over orzo from 150 g uncooked. Nyusika: ≈280 g prawns with 30 g feta over orzo from 35 g uncooked.

notes: Cook any day this week (prawns from the freezer keep). Kifli usually has frozen raw king prawns; if only cooked prawns are available, add them with the feta and just heat through.
